item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While the mental image did make me chuckle, I'm not sure how I feel about this an as SCP. While this is a nice change to the "how many unanswered questions can be crammed into an article" approach that many writers seem to use, it still feels too dull. Why is the Foundation even bothering to research this? Seems like a waste of resources. I suppose it would be interesting to weaponize this, turning it into some sort of grenade. Or orbital laser. Actually, anything that could lead to the development of an orbital snakes-out-of-your-face cannon can't be a waste.

Anyway, although the concept is creative, I just don't see any way to make this less… meh.

"Researchers are to be reminded that SCP-815 acts on the nearest person, even when opened by robot. I don't want to have to keep cleaning up these accidents, people."

I guess retarted researchers is a bit of an overstatement here, given some of the stuff that makes it into these. You'd really think they'd modify the security measures stringently to prevent that sort of thing after the first or second time it happened (the way it's written suggests this is a repeat problem).

What happens to the old ones?
